reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: src/jump.rs owns stack navigation counters and copied positions, while input, position table and rendering allocations remain external owners. jump_loc coordinates those APIs rather than acquiring a separate table.
owner_creation.invariant: A copied jump destination carries no backing-storage lifetime.
limitations: No heap owner is created by the local POSITION variables.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/jump.rs combines next_unfiltered, screen index conversion and current on-screen position before scrolling. The same active file and geometry must remain selected throughout that composite operation.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A destination must be revalidated against current file and screen state.
limitations: The raw/scalar interfaces carry no file-generation proof.

callback_targets.analysis: src/jump.rs directly invokes forw/back, repaint_hilite and input seek APIs; jump_line_loc finds a raw line boundary with ch_back_get before handing the position to jump_loc.
callback_targets.invariant: Navigation callees must not invalidate active input assumptions mid-call.
limitations: There is no retained callback context providing an owner guard.

invalidation.analysis: src/jump.rs jump_forw calls lastmark and pos_clear before rebuilding the bottom-of-file view. Old screen positions are logically invalid even though their scalar values and table address can remain unchanged.
invalidation.invariant: Clearing a screen view retires its old coordinate interpretation.
limitations: The backing table lifecycle is reviewed separately in OWN-07.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/jump.rs can clear positions and the screen before deciding which scrolling path to use. It then updates display/navigation state through separate calls with no rollback frame object.
mutation_commit.invariant: A jump commit must preserve coherence across position and displayed content.
limitations: M0-MEM-001 records this shared-state contract without a new failure reproduction.

release_pair.analysis: src/jump.rs borrows input and position services and contains no local free/close in these navigation paths. lastmark stores navigation metadata through another owner rather than transferring an allocation here.
release_pair.invariant: Borrowed position and input resources must remain with their owners.
limitations: A completed jump does not prove process-level release of those resources.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/jump.rs reports failed end seek or destination seek and returns; it does not locally restore every earlier screen or position mutation performed by the composite jump.
error_cleanup.invariant: Failed navigation must not be described as an untouched owner transaction.
limitations: No extra heap rollback is needed for its own stack values.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/jump.rs relies on serialized calls into mutable navigation, filter and render state. It registers no handler and encodes no exclusive handoff; M0-MEM-001 stays open for these cross-owner assumptions.
signals_handoff.invariant: Input identity and navigation geometry must remain coherent until return.
limitations: This review does not trace an asynchronous route into jump_loc itself.
